subtitle: Beneath the Green Domes of Charaideo

panels.shot: wide aerial sunset shot over rolling green mounds and broken brick walls on a misty Assam hilltop
panels.action: Chang-Rung Phukan and Rudra Singha stand small against a landscape of earthen domes and crumbling octagonal brick enclosures at Charaideo, as clouds cast long shadows over the ancient maidams.

dialogue.text: On the hill of Charaideo, where Tai chiefs slept under earth and brick, an architect and a king quietly rewrote how the Ahoms would remember the dead.

i18n.hi: चराइदेव की पहाड़ी पर, जहाँ ताई सरदार मिट्टी और ईंट के नीचे सोए, एक स्थापति और राजा ने चुपचाप तय किया कि अहोम मौत को कैसे याद करेंगे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on one massive maidam mound rising from early-morning fog, with forest beyond
panels.action: The grassy dome of a great maidam swells from the mist, its rounded form smooth and silent, while distant hills and sal trees frame the lonely hill of Charaideo.

dialogue.text: Here, from the thirteenth to the eighteenth century, the Ahom rulers raised earthen domes over brick vaults, turning Charaideo into a city of the dead that watched over a living kingdom.

i18n.hi: यहीं, तेरहवीं से अठारहवीं सदी तक, अहोम शासकों ने ईंट की कोठरियों पर मिट्टी के गुंबद उठाए, चराइदेव को ज़िंदा राज्य पर नज़र रखती मृतकों की नगरी बना दिया।

panels.shot: cutaway wide shot imagining an early 13th-century scene, slightly elevated angle over a small Tai-Ahom settlement
panels.action: In a flashback scene, Tai-Ahom settlers clear a forested hill; a freshly built low earthen mound rises beside wooden houses, while elders in plain robes perform a simple burial rite.

dialogue.text: In the early days, when the Tai-Ahom chiefs first chose Charaideo as their capital, their burials were humbler, closer to their south-east Asian homelands, yet already set apart on the sacred hill.

i18n.hi: जब ताई-अहोम सरदारों ने पहली बार चराइदेव को राजधानी चुना, उनकी समाधियाँ साधारण थीं, अपने दक्षिण-पूर्व एशियाई घरों जैसी, पर फिर भी इस पवित्र पहाड़ी पर अलग ठहराई गईं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Chang-Rung Phukan seated indoors at a low table, manuscripts and tools spread around, lit by lamplight
panels.action: Chang-Rung Phukan leans over palm-leaf manuscripts, stylus in hand, measuring rods and a small brick model of a vault beside him as he carefully writes the procedures for tomb construction.

dialogue.text: Generations later, the Chang-Rung Phukan, the royal architect, gathered what practice and memory knew into a buranji, setting down how a maidam must rise, brick by brick, ritual by ritual.

i18n.hi: पीढ़ियों बाद, चांग-रुंग फुकन, राज स्थापति, ने अभ्यास और याद को बुरंजी में जोड़ा, लिख दिया कि मैदाम कैसे उठेगा, ईंट पर ईंट, अनुष्ठान पर अनुष्ठान।

panels.shot: cutaway cross-section wide shot, half above ground and half below, showing the internal structure of a maidam
panels.action: A cutaway vision reveals an underground brick-vaulted chamber with pillars and niches, an earthen mound swelling above, and an enclosing octagonal brick wall encircling the silent structure.

dialogue.text: The buranji describes a buried brick chamber, sometimes with multiple rooms and pillars, sealed and covered by earth, then ringed by an octagonal wall: a palace for the dead beneath a green dome.

i18n.hi: बुरंजी एक दबी ईंटी कोठरी का वर्णन करती है, कभी कई कमरों और स्तंभों वाली, जिसे बंद कर मिट्टी से ढका जाता, फिर अष्टकोणीय दीवार से घेरा जाता: हरी गुंबद के नीचे मृतकों का महल।

panels.shot: low-angle wide shot of labourers constructing an octagonal wall in brick, forest and sky beyond
panels.action: Rows of workers lift and place fired bricks in an emerging octagonal ring, while overseers gesture; in the center, a half-finished earthen mound rises over a hidden vault.

dialogue.text: Brickmakers, masons and earth-workers turned the architect’s lines into walls and mounds, so that each Ahom king and noble would lie within a carefully measured geometry of power and memory.

i18n.hi: ईंटसाज़, राजमिस्त्री और मिट्टी-कारिगर ने स्थापति की रेखाओं को दीवारों और टीलों में बदला, ताकि हर अहोम राजा और सरदार शक्ति और स्मृति की नापी-तुली ज्यामिति में लेटें।

panels.shot: dim interior medium shot inside a newly completed vault, lit by oil lamps, with attendants placing objects
panels.action: Inside the brick vault, attendants arrange wooden ritual objects and carved ivory panels near a central resting place, their faces solemn in the flickering lamplight.

dialogue.text: The Ahom chronicles speak of treasured objects sent below; centuries later, excavations at a maidam would uncover ivory panels and wooden pieces, echoes of those recorded funeral furnishings.

i18n.hi: अहोम बुरंजियाँ उन ख़ज़ानों का ज़िक्र करती हैं जो नीचे भेजे गए; सदियों बाद, एक मैदाम की खुदाई में हाथीदाँत की पट्टियाँ और लकड़ी के टुकड़े मिले, उन लिखी अन्त्येष्टि वस्तुओं की गूँज।

panels.shot: wide ritual courtyard shot, with priests and officials arrayed around the maidam, river valley visible in distance
panels.action: On the slope of Charaideo, priests and royal officers stand facing a newly raised maidam, smoke from offerings curling upward as drums and conches lie silent at their feet.

dialogue.text: Around the maidams, officers held titles tied to the dead, and rites linked the buried rulers with the living realm, for the Ahoms believed that kings did not simply vanish beneath the hill.

i18n.hi: मैदामों के चारों ओर अफसरों के पद खुद मृतकों से जुड़े थे, और अनुष्ठान दफन राजाओं को ज़िंदा राज्य से बाँधते थे, क्योंकि अहोम मानते थे कि राजा पहाड़ी के नीचे बस यूँ ही ग़ायब नहीं हो जाते।

panels.shot: tight medium shot of a small group of bound attendants near a burial site, faces fearful, guards impassive
panels.action: A group of attendants stand with hands loosely bound, eyes wide with dread, as guards and officials look on near the mouth of a half-sealed vault.

dialogue.text: Yet the same texts also whisper of a darker duty: in earlier times, some attendants were sent alive into the vault, buried with their lord, the ultimate sign of loyalty and a terrible cost.

i18n.hi: पर वही ग्रंथ एक काले फ़र्ज़ की फुसफुसाहट भी करते हैं: पुराने समय में कुछ सेवक ज़िंदा ही कोठरी में उतारे गए, अपने स्वामी के साथ दफन, निष्ठा की चरम निशानी और भयानक कीमत।

panels.shot: dramatic throne-room medium shot of Rudra Singha, slightly low angle, courtiers around, heavy beams overhead
panels.action: Rudra Singha sits upright on a carved throne, hand raised in firm decision, as courtiers exchange tense glances in the wooden hall of the Ahom court.

dialogue.text: When Rudra Singha ruled in the early eighteenth century, the buranjis credit him with a quiet revolution: he ordered that no more living attendants be buried with their masters at Charaideo.

i18n.hi: अठारहवीं सदी की शुरुआत में, जब रुद्र सिंघा राज कर रहे थे, बुरंजियाँ उन्हें एक शांत क्रांति का श्रेय देती हैं: उन्होंने आदेश दिया कि चराइदेव में अब किसी ज़िंदा सेवक को स्वामी के साथ न दफनाया जाए।

panels.shot: medium two-shot of Rudra Singha speaking to Chang-Rung Phukan in a shaded courtyard overlooking distant maidams
panels.action: Rudra Singha stands beside Chang-Rung Phukan, pointing toward the hazy line of maidam domes on the horizon, while the architect listens intently, scrolls in his hands.

dialogue.speaker: the_chang_rung_phukan_and_rudra_singha
dialogue.text: Let the bricks stand, Phukan, but let the living walk out into the sun.

i18n.hi: "ईंटें खड़ी रहने दो, फुकन, पर ज़िंदा लोग धूप में बाहर लौटें।"

panels.shot: symbolic medium shot of labourers sealing a vault entrance with bricks while freed attendants walk away toward the light
panels.action: At the entrance of a vault, masons calmly lay the final bricks, while nearby a small group of former attendants, unbound, step away toward the hillside path, faces turned to the sky.

dialogue.text: In the architect’s practice, little changed in brick or earth; but in the lives spared at the door of the vault, the kingdom altered its pact with death while keeping faith with remembrance.

i18n.hi: स्थापति की कारीगरी में न ईंट बदली, न मिट्टी; पर जो जानें कोठरी के द्वार पर बचीं, उनमें राज्य ने मौत से अपना सौदा बदला, याद से समझौता किए बिना।

panels.shot: wide shot of a maidam centuries later, partially damaged, with a gaping hole in the mound and scattered bricks
panels.action: A weathered maidam shows a collapsed section where looters once broke through, bricks tumbled and grass torn, the octagonal wall breached by an old scar.

dialogue.text: Time and greed carved their own passages; when archaeologists entered one maidam in our age, they met not untouched stillness but disturbed earth and a vault already wounded by looters.

i18n.hi: समय और लालच ने अपनी सुरंगें खोदीं; जब हमारे दौर के पुरातत्वविदों ने एक मैदाम खोला, उन्हें अनछुई शांति नहीं, उखड़ी मिट्टी और पहले से ही लुटेरों से ज़ख्मी कोठरी मिली।

panels.shot: careful interior medium shot of modern archaeologists inside the vault, kneeling by skeletal remains and objects, soft lantern light
panels.action: Modern archaeologists in simple field clothes kneel inside the brick chamber, gently brushing soil from skeletal remains and ivory panels, recording each detail under the glow of portable lamps.

dialogue.text: Even so, the excavation at one maidam revealed five skeletons, ivory and wooden pieces, traces that broadly matched the buranji’s words, though many questions about each tomb still remain.

i18n.hi: फिर भी, एक मैदाम की खुदाई में पाँच कंकाल, हाथीदाँत और लकड़ी के टुकड़े मिले, निशान जो मोटे तौर पर बुरंजी की बातों से मिलते थे, भले हर समाधि पर कई सवाल अभी बाकी हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a present-day Me-Dam-Me-Phi ceremony at the foot of the hill, families gathered, offerings laid out
panels.action: Modern Assamese men and women sit and stand around an altar under the open sky, offering rice, flowers and incense during Me-Dam-Me-Phi, while the distant mounds of Charaideo rise behind them.

dialogue.text: Each year, in Me-Dam-Me-Phi rites, the living still call upon ancestors, the Ahom tradition of honouring the dead carried forward without burial chambers, turning hill and home into shared sacred space.

i18n.hi: हर साल मे-दम-मे-फी के अनुष्ठानों में, ज़िंदा लोग अब भी पूर्वजों को पुकारते हैं, अहोम परंपरा बिना दफन कोठरियों के जारी है, पहाड़ी और घर, दोनों को साझा पवित्र जगह बना देती है।

panels.shot: contemporary aerial wide shot of Charaideo maidams, with visitors walking on paths and conservation structures visible
panels.action: From above, the preserved maidam mounds and their brick outlines stretch across Charaideo, as small groups of visitors and conservators move along marked paths between the green domes.

dialogue.text: In 2023, the world formally recognised Charaideo’s maidams, yet most lie unexcavated beneath their grass, their stories known only in part, their silence protected as much as it is studied.

i18n.hi: 2023 में दुनिया ने चराइदेव के मैदामों को औपचारिक मान्यता दी, पर ज़्यादातर अब भी घास के नीचे अनखुदे हैं, उनकी कहानियाँ आधी-अधूरी जानी जाती हैं, उनकी ख़ामोशी जितनी पढ़ी जाती है उतनी ही बचाई भी जाती है।

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot of Chang-Rung Phukan and Rudra Singha imagined standing together on a modern path between maidams, blending past and present
panels.action: An imaginative scene shows Chang-Rung Phukan and Rudra Singha gazing over the maidams as they appear today, their figures ghostlike yet solid, watching visitors who pass unaware between the domes.

dialogue.text: Between the architect’s measured bricks and the king’s choice to spare lives, Charaideo teaches that a people can build mighty tombs, yet honour their dead best by loosening death’s hold on the living.

i18n.hi: स्थापति की नापी हुई ईंटों और राजा के प्राण बचाने के फ़ैसले के बीच, चराइदेव सिखाता है कि लोग महान समाधियाँ बना सकते हैं, पर अपने मृतकों का सबसे अच्छा सम्मान तब करते हैं जब ज़िंदा लोगों पर मौत की पकड़ ढीली करते हैं।

title_i18n.en: The Maidams of Charaideo Remember the Dead
title_i18n.hi: चराइदेव के मैदाम, मृतकों की याद

subtitle_i18n.hi: चराइदेव की हरी गुंबदों के नीचे
